thesis: Diagnose financial behavior patterns and choose a small corrective action.
summary: Six archetypes are martyr, speculator, avoider, hoarder, trapped employee and apathetic. Suggested exercises include auditing unwanted sacrifices, committing to one opportunity, reviewing abandoned projects, a five-minute financial check, a small investment, a six-month exit fund and a thirty-day learning focus. She rejects suffering as a wealth mechanism while endorsing interest-driven effort. Newsletter promotion sits within the discussion.

insights.title: Audit whether sacrifices serve anyone
insights.explanation: Her martyr exercise asks who requested a sacrifice and whether it creates wealth, then suggests delegating, deleting or changing it.

review_status: Codex editorial draft; complete local transcript read; claims not independently verified
synthesis_method: Direct Codex extraction from complete local transcript; exact quotations verified locally
context_and_limits: Archetypes are editorial devices, not diagnoses or proof poverty is caused by beliefs. Historical, psychological, trading-study and biography claims are unverified. She explicitly says employment is acceptable and does not advise quitting tomorrow. The hoarder exercise includes buying education, not solely financial securities; her cash allocation is personal.
review_changes: Restores the anti-burnout message, exit-runway safeguard and difference between obsession and generic overwork.
